spans.s: or श॑र्दिस् (of unknown meaning), AV. xviii, 3, 16.
(of unknown derivation) a tiger, VS. &c. &c.
a lion, L.
a panther, leopard, L.
the fabulous animal Śarabha, L.
a kind of bird, L.
any eminent person, best, excellent, pre-eminent (ifc.; cf. व्याघ्र), MBh.; Kāv. &c.
Plumbago Zeylanica, L.
N. of two metres (cf. below), Col.
of a Rākṣasa, R.
pl. N. of a Śākhā or school of the Yajur-veda
(ई), f. a tigress (also the mythical mother of tigers and other beasts of prey), MBh.; R.
शार्दूल—कर्ण m. N. of a son of Tri-śaṅku, Buddh.
शार्दूल—चर्म॑न् n. a tiger's skin, TBr.
शार्दूल॑—ज्येष्ठ (शार्दुल॑-), mfn. having a tiger as superior or chief, ŚBr.
शार्दूल—मृग-सेवित mfn. frequented by tigers and deer, MBh.
शार्दूल—ललित n. ‘tiger's sport’, N. of a metre (consisting of four Pādas of 19 syllables each), Col.
शार्दूल—लोम॑न् n. tiger's hair, ŚBr.
शार्दूल—वर्मन् m. N. of a king, Inscr.
शार्दूल—वाहन m. ‘riding on a tiger’, N. of Mañju-śrī, L.
शार्दूल—विक्रीडित n. ‘tiger's play’, N. of a metre (consisting of four Pādas of 19 syllables each), Gīt.; Śrutab.; Chandom. (also mfn. imitating a tiger's play).
शार्दूल—शतक n. N. of a poem.
शार्दूल—सम-विक्रम mfn. having prowess equal to a tiger, as bold as a tiger, MW.
a facetious expression for the female organ, TS.
N. of a preceptor, Lāṭy.
wet, moist, damp, MBh.; Naiṣ.
